metadata.note: The Central New England Railway and its predecessors, drawn by operating company: Hartford and Connecticut Western (1881-1889), Central New England and Western (1889-1892), Philadelphia, Reading and New England (1892-1899), Central New England Railway (1899-1926), Rhinebeck and Connecticut (1875-1882), Dutchess and Columbia (1870-1877) and Newburgh, Dutchess and Connecticut (1877-1905), and the New York, New Haven and Hartford's operation of the ex-CNE passenger services after the 1927 merger (to 1927, 1928 and 9 Sep 1933). Lines: Hartford - Winsted - Canaan - State Line; State Line - Millerton; Rhinecliff - Silvernails - Copake - Boston Corners - State Line; the Poughkeepsie & Connecticut line and the later consolidated Poughkeepsie - Stissing - Pine Plains - Silvernails route; Poughkeepsie Bridge - Campbell Hall; Poughkeepsie - Hopewell Junction - Danbury; Dutchess Junction / Beacon - Pine Plains - Millerton; the Springfield Branch. Every span drawn is the research report's drawable: span. Research report: research/branches/central_new_england_railway.txt.
metadata.operator_split: Rule 4: features sharing geometry split at each change of operator - 31 Mar 1881 (CW -> H&CW; the CW era is the separate connecticut_western_railroad entry), 16 Jun 1882 (R&C -> H&CW; 1 Jul per WCNE), Aug 1889 (H&CW lease to the CNE&W), 1 Aug 1892 (CNE&W -> PR&NE), 23 Jan 1899 (PR&NE -> CNE), 14 Sep 1905 (ND&C -> CNE operation; the 25 Jun 1907 formal merger is not a second split), and the 1927 merger into the New Haven (1 Jan per WCNE, 10 May per BLK - CONFLICT): every CNE feature ends 1926 and every New Haven feature starts 1927, so the disputed months fall on the New Haven side without any year being drawn twice. NOT splits: the PR&NE receivership of Aug 1893 (the same company's receivers) and the New Haven's stock control of the CNE from early 1904 (the CNE kept running its own trains - WCNE, WRC, and in 1925 PAT). Boundary years elsewhere appear on both sides because both companies ran trains that year. Colours: the six predecessor companies and the CNE had no colour in data/, so new hexes were chosen that no other company uses; the New Haven colour is read programmatically from the existing New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad features.

Merger date into the New Haven: 1 Jan 1927 (WCNE) vs 10 May 1927 (BLK).

Connecticut end date: only 'late/December 1927' (WRC/Karr p.138, CAN, NOR); no exact last train, and no per-segment end for Hartford - Tariffville, the Springfield Branch or the Collinsville spur. Karr 2017 pp.134-140 and Ashman & Milmine 1972 would settle it.

Springfield Branch: WCNE says the Massachusetts part was abandoned in 1921; a rootsweb history (snippet) says trains still reached Feeding Hills later (freight); Fowler shows Agawam Jct only in 1904 but Feeding Hills in 1920. CONFLICT.
Poughkeepsie - Campbell Hall passenger end: confirmed only to June 1921; could be any time 1921-1927.
Dutchess County RR operator 1892-1907, and whether New Haven crews ran it after the 1 Dec 1904 lease assignment.
R&C opening 4 Apr (WRC) vs 14 Apr 1875 (WCNE); R&C -> H&CW 16 Jun (WRC) vs 1 Jul 1882 (WCNE, Robinson); H&CW purchase of Boston Corners - State Line 1 Apr (WRC) vs 1 Sep 1884 (Robinson).

segments.note: Hartford - Bloomfield - Tariffville - Simsbury (Hoskins) - Canton - Collinsville Junction - New Hartford - Winsted - Norfolk - East Canaan - Canaan - Salisbury - Lakeville - State Line. The Connecticut Western was reorganized as the Hartford and Connecticut Western on 31 Mar 1881 (WCNE), trains running on unbroken from the CW era; the H&CW ran them until it was leased to the Central New England and Western in Aug 1889 (WRC, citing McLaughlin and Robinson). A Philadelphia & Reading-associated syndicate held control from 1887 - stock only, the H&CW still operated (WRC). Positive H&CW-era evidence: from March 1883 the H&CW routed its trains State Line - Millerton - Boston Corners (WRC) and Fowler cites an 1888 H&CW timetable (FSNE lines 127/147). The 1871-1881 Connecticut Western era belongs to the separate connecticut_western_railroad entry and is not drawn here. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

segments.note: [OPEN] Feeding Hills - Agawam Junction on the CNE's own rails, then 4.1 mi into Springfield (Union Station) by trackage rights over the Boston & Albany (WCNE; FSNE line 148). Opened 12 Sep 1902 (WCNE). Agawam Jct carries only Fowler's a (1904) letter (FSNE line 148), so passenger service is confirmed to 1904. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when this service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. The upper bound is the 1921 abandonment of the Massachusetts part (WCNE); a rootsweb history says trains still reached Feeding Hills from Hartford later (freight; snippet only) - CONFLICT on the Massachusetts end, recorded in metadata. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
